html:
SMTO-SKL-0110 — SMTO can't find the Slack app setup it needs

GUID: 31450d9b-154a-52b2-acb8-d24f653baaf2
Slug: slack-oauth-app-missing
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • To connect Slack, SMTO needs a saved Slack OAuth App entry holding your Slack app's details. The name used, or the one a saved Slack connection points to, doesn't exist. Nothing was sent to Slack.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store from the More options menu and search for slack. Look for an entry made from the Slack OAuth App template and check its name against the one you used. SMTO looks up the Slack app by its exact name, so a small typo makes it look missing.
  2. If there's no such entry, ask the person who manages SMTO to create one from the Slack OAuth App template. If a Slack connection used to work, give it the same name as before. A saved Slack connection remembers its app by name, so the new entry must use that name for it to keep working.
  3. Ask SMTO to connect Slack with that app, typing @ in the message box and picking the entry, then finish Slack's page in your browser. Picking the entry with @ gives SMTO its exact name, so nothing is guessed.

What success looks like

  • The Slack sign-in tab shows a message starting with "Connected" that says you can close the window.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the Slack app's client secret into a conversation; it belongs only in the Parameter Store entry.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • SlackProfiles.resolve found no Parameter Store record under the requested exact slack_oauth_app key (the auth_app_ref given to slack.connect, or a saved workspace's oauth_app_ref during use or token refresh).

What this means

  • Exact OAuth app lookup finds no saved Slack app profile. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Exact OAuth app lookup finds no saved Slack app profile.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect auth_app_ref and the intended Parameter Store entry.

How to fix it

  • Create a profile from the "Slack OAuth App" template in Parameter Store (client_id, client_secret, flow, explicit scopes, HTTPS redirect_uri ending /api/agent/slack/oauth/callback) and pass its exact key as auth_app_ref to slack.connect; aliases and display names are not resolved. If a saved slack_workspace fails with this, restore the app record under the key named in that workspace's oauth_app_ref.
  • Create and save a Slack OAuth App in Parameter Store, then pass its exact auth_app_ref to slack.connect.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported Slack OAuth app profile exists before connect starts.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
